overview.lead: Paladins heal, tank and fight in melee. Blizzard's intent: Holy is the strongest single-target healer, Protection a tank with strong cooldowns and better control, and Retribution a damage dealer whose group value comes mainly from keeping Judgements up.

points.text: For Olympus (Alliance), Paladins are Human or Dwarf. The 26 Oct racial changes swapped Dwarf's Earth Fury for Artisan's Precision (+1% hit) and cut Human's Ruthless crit bonus from 2% to 1%.
Blizzard lists the class's edges and gaps: very strong against Undead and Demons, limited range that Holy talents extend, no interrupt and no way to slow enemies.

101.summary: What every Paladin should know before choosing a spec.

overview.lead: Holy is the Paladin healer. Blizzard wants it to be the strongest single-target healer, with group healing that takes more planning, and calls Paladins viable healers in all group content.

points.text: Holy builds around Holy Shock and Light's Vigil. Oath of Light improves your direct healing on one ally, while Boundless Light improves Holy Shock crit on allies without your Oath.
Blizzard also supports a Holy Shock hybrid ('Shockadin'); Warcraft Tavern says it is too early to judge it.

101.summary: Leveling, the core rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: Spiritual Focus is now on row 1 and Divine Favor on row 3. Holy Shock remains a key heal. Voice of Truth was removed from the Holy tree.
Redemption comes from 'The Tome of Divinity' at 12; Consecration and Blessing of Kings are trained at 20.
Holy Strike (level 6) gives every Paladin an instant Holy-damage attack for solo play.
Dual Specialization at level 40 lets you keep Retribution or Protection for questing.
Heal with Flash of Light and Holy Light. Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits shorten your next Holy Light (Infusion of Light).
Holy Shock heals an ally or hits an enemy on a 10 s cooldown; keep it for targets that drop fast.
Light's Vigil: place it on an ally (30 s). Your next Holy Shock on them has no cooldown and heals their whole party at once.
Divine Favor makes your next Flash of Light, Holy Light or Holy Shock a guaranteed crit, which also feeds Illumination's mana refund.
Keep your assigned Blessing and Aura active. Coordinate your Oath of Light target with the other healers.
Divine Precision shortens Silence. Save instant Holy Shock or move behind cover when a caster is waiting to interrupt.
Lay on Hands is on a 20-minute cooldown in Forever (was 1 hour), so don't hoard it.
Purifying Power makes Cleanse and Purify cheaper, which adds up in fights with a lot of dispelling.
Spiritual Focus protects Flash of Light, Holy Light and Light's Vigil from pushback, and Reverence keeps part of your mana regen going while you cast.

201.summary: Stat priorities, raid duties, consumables and PvP.

steps.text: Divine Precision reduces time spent silenced. Purifying Power sits on row 2 and helps make Cleanse cheaper.
Hammer of Justice is your main stun. Paladins have no gap closer, interrupt or slow, so stay close to your team.
Unyielding Faith shortens Fear and Disorient effects on you (15% at rank 1).
Against Mage: Against a Mage, make room for a cast by using cover or waiting out the interrupt. Divine Precision reduces time spent silenced.
Against Priest: Forever Priests get Silence without a talent prerequisite. Divine Precision reduces its duration, so plan instant heals around the Priest's control.
Against Warlock: Unyielding Faith shortens their Fear. Warcraft Tavern notes Warlocks have no blink or sprint, so once your team reaches them they struggle to get away.

overview.lead: Protection is the Paladin tank. Warcraft Tavern calls it a real, working tank for the first time, thanks to the Seal of Fury taunt and Templar's Bulwark.

points.text: Seal of Fury (level 10) adds Holy damage to each swing plus an absorb worth half of it, and judging it taunts from 10 yards.
Consecration deals full damage to the first four enemies. Holy Shield is now on row 5 and adds block chance and Holy damage on blocks.

101.summary: Leveling, the core rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: Train Righteous Fury at level 10. Improved Seal of Fury is gone, so plan mana around current tools such as Shield Specialization.
Redoubt raises your block chance after melee hits, and Shield Specialization lets blocks restore mana.
Forever adds nine new dungeons from level 13 to 60, starting with The Hall of Thanes in Ironforge (13-18).
Templar's Bulwark moved to row 3 and Holy Shield moved to row 5.
Keep Righteous Fury and Seal of Fury active; judge to taunt or pull from 10 yards (Judgement no longer uses up the Seal).
Use Consecration on packs and Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s); Iron Creed makes Holy Strike add threat and briefly cut your damage taken.
Keep Holy Shield up when melee hits are coming: more block for 10 s or 4 blocks, with Holy damage on each block.
Save Templar's Bulwark (an absorb equal to your max health for 8 s, 5-minute cooldown) for spikes; it applies Forbearance.
Swift Judgement releases your active Seal on its own cooldown. Plan your next taunt without relying on a Judgement reset.
Templar's Bulwark applies Forbearance for 1 minute and cannot be cast while Forbearance is active.
Sacred Duty shortens the cooldowns of Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark and reduces Forbearance duration. It no longer adds Stamina.
Paladins have no interrupt; Hammer of Justice is your stun, and Improved Hammer of Justice shortens its cooldown.
Reckoning stores up to 4 extra attacks from blocks and crits taken, and releases them all on your next auto-attack.

omitted.reason: The spec overview above covers this.

201.summary: Stat priorities, raid duties, consumables and PvP.

steps.text: Blizzard designed Protection as a tank with strong cooldowns and better control. In PvP, Templar's Bulwark absorbs a burst and Hammer of Justice is your stun.
Holy Strike's pure Holy damage ignores armor (Warcraft Tavern), and Seal of Fury's absorb soaks part of incoming hits.

overview.lead: Retribution is the Paladin melee damage spec. Blizzard says its group value comes mainly from keeping Judgements up on the target.

points.text: Unsealed Wrath is the 31-point choice and requires Repentance. It stores your active Seal on melee hits, then uses the stored stacks when you land a hit with a different Seal.
Sacred Arbiter (16 points) adds 20% Holy Strike damage and makes Holy Strike refresh every Judgement on the target, including other Paladins'.

101.summary: Leveling, the core rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: At 20, 'The Tome of Valor' leads to Verigan's Fist, a two-handed mace that suits Two-Handed Weapon Specialization.
Pursuit of Justice raises run and mounted speed (8% at rank 1) but does not stack with other speed effects.
Benediction makes instant spells cheaper, and Sanctified Judgement can return part of a judged Seal's mana.
Repentance (21 points) incapacitates a Humanoid for up to 6 s; Warcraft Tavern sees it mainly as a PvP tool.
Keep a Seal active (Seal of Command once you have it) and judge on cooldown.
Use Holy Strike on cooldown (10 s); with Sacred Arbiter it also refreshes Judgements.
With Unsealed Wrath, build stored Seal stacks on melee hits, then switch Seals and land a hit before the stacks expire.
Use Consecration when you need area damage. Holy Conduit is now in Holy, so check your mana before using expensive area spells.
Judgement no longer consumes your Seal, so you never recast a Seal just to judge again.
Vindication lowers the target's Attack Power and raises yours for 30 s (68 and 1% at rank 1).
Eye for an Eye returns 5% of crit damage you take to the attacker (rank 1), capped at half your health.
Dwarf's new Artisan's Precision racial adds 1% hit with spells and attacks.

omitted.reason: The spec overview above covers this.

201.summary: Stat priorities, raid duties, consumables and PvP.

steps.text: Warcraft Tavern sees Repentance (21 points) mainly as a PvP talent. Eye for an Eye also punishes crits against you (5% of the damage at rank 1).
Holy Strike's pure Holy damage ignores armor, and Hammer of Justice is your main stun (Warcraft Tavern).
You have no gap closer; Pursuit of Justice is a passive speed bonus that does not stack with other speed effects.
Against Mage: Blizzard calls Mages fragile in melee but strong at control, Polymorph included; Hammer of Justice and Repentance give you control back.
Against Warlock: Warcraft Tavern notes Warlocks have no blink or sprint, so Pursuit of Justice and Hammer of Justice keep you on them.
